newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building wage talks deferrred to April 11.
newsitem.headline: German building wage talks deferrred to April 11.

text.p: The latest round of wage talks for Germany's 1.3 million building industry workers ended without agreement on Wednesday and talks were deferred until April 11, the IG Bau union and employers' representatives said.
Wilhelm Kuechler, negotiator for the construction industry, said differences over wage demands and over the payment of the so-called "thirteenth month" wage remained entrenched.
IG Bau leader Klaus Wiesehuegel said he was pessimistic, but said no-one had wanted to break off talks prematurely.
However both sides said there had been some rapprochement over the contentious issue on how to deal with the annual surge in building sector joblessness during winter months.
That issue had been expected to be a key bone of contention.

Already this year, winter construction unemployment is calculated to have accounted for nearly half of the 510,000 jump in January joblessness that helped push overall German unemployment levels to post-war records.

That was itself partly a result of a government move last winter to scrap "poor weather" payments to building employees, which had allowed them to be retained by their firms even when there was no work.
In their place, employer and union representatives were obliged to negotiate agreements under which firms pay their staff "bridging money" in times of poor weather.
But these bridging agreements have proved too expensive for firms and the vast majority do not pay them, preferring instead to lay off staff during winter and later use cheaper foreign labour.
IG Bau, the construction trade union, has not yet set a definite wage demand in the talks, saying only that it wants to ensure that salaries do not fall in real terms.
